purpose: Build one trait-blind present-environment pipeline for orientation, phyllary posture and involucre stickiness using the same occurrence QC, thinning and CHELSA variables.

environment.selection_rule: Use the four CHELSA variables already frozen for Chapter 2 before this cross-trait comparison; do not add or remove predictors after seeing results.

occurrence.note: Japan is the population-provenance frame of the Japan38 nuclear-tip analysis, not a biological region class. No Japan-versus-Taiwan country contrast is used as a biological predictor.

analysis.taxon_summary: median CHELSA value across thinned occurrences
analysis.trait_test: For each trait and environment variable, compare observed between-state separation with all unique state-label permutations preserving observed state counts. For multistate phyllary posture use the median pairwise distance between state centroids in standardized environment space as the omnibus statistic.
analysis.primary_rule: Report complete finite ranks and state coverage. Do not convert coverage failure into a null ecological conclusion.
analysis.cross_trait_rule: Compare ecological evaluability and finite-rank patterns across all three traits without forcing equal taxon counts or borrowing orientation-specific BIO15/BIO1 direction hypotheses.

claim_ceiling: Present-environment correspondence is not adaptation, selection or historical cause.
Taxon-level authority states are not measured at each occurrence coordinate.
Phyllary results with one taxon in a state are resolution-limited even if a finite rank can be computed.
The one-occurrence phyllary sensitivity is diagnostic only and cannot replace the primary >=3-occurrence gate.
No country boundary is treated as an ecological region boundary.
